# Native OpenSim Marker Geometry

This provisional calculation pathway belongs to F07/F08 and scoped child
#11903. It does not qualify anatomical calibration, capture matching or
independent dynamics. The [native muscle replay chapter](13-native-muscle-replay.qmd)
retains the separate full-state, actuation and native-contact gates.

## Inputs, Frames and Identity

`tour_matching.native_marker_geometry.NativeMarkerGeometry` loads an explicit
OpenSim model and distinct absolute native coordinate paths. Bindings pair each
observed label with an existing absolute body-attached `PhysicalFrame` path
and a finite local station offset in metres. Coordinate values use native SI
units (metres/radians); no body-name alias, marker correspondence, world-axis
registration or anthropometric calibration is inferred.

Source bytes, loaded native serialization, runtime version, native simulation
extension, provider source, selected coordinates and numerical policies enter
the identity. This does not pin the entire dependent DLL/resource closure.
Structural counts do not establish anatomical coverage or correct muscle paths.
Source model muscles, forces, locks, constraints and parameters remain intact.

## Position Calculation and Assembly

Each evaluation starts from a copy of the initialized native state, sets only
selected independent coordinates, calls native assembly and realizes position.
Locked, prescribed and dependent selected coordinates are rejected. All assembled
coordinates must remain in their source ranges. Selected achieved values must
match requests within $10^{-7}$ native units; other independent coordinates must
retain their initial values. Dependents follow the actual native constraints.
The explicit assembly accuracy is $10^{-14}$. These are numerical policies,
not physiological or measurement tolerances.

For local station $s_b$, the world position is
$p_W=R_{Wb}s_b+t_{Wb}$. Native `findStationLocationInGround` is checked against
the frame-transform calculation. Native body poses replace the previous
identity-pose/raw-offset placeholders. Metadata-only plants now reject physical
geometry requests. Closure and dynamics stepping remain unavailable and raise;
zero closure or an unchanged state cannot stand in for native computation.
The IK adapter supplies a real `pose_fn` for shared trajectory fitting; its
generic grip/ground `solve_pose` pathway is not implemented or qualified.

## Bounded Shared Trajectory Fit

The existing `solve_full_body_ik_trajectory` minimizes observed marker residuals
and the existing warm-start regularizer $w_r(q-q_{previous})$. An explicit
finite lower/upper bound pair selects SciPy TRF; omission retains the previous
LM behavior. Invalid bounds or an out-of-bounds initial pose are rejected,
without clipping or widening the model. Native assembly checks still apply at
every evaluated configuration. Finite output and optimizer stopping do not
establish feasibility or convergence; residuals remain mandatory evidence.
The bounded path disables cost-only stopping, matching the existing pose TRF
policy, so an initial tiny step from an active bound is not mistaken for convergence.

The bounded diagnostic reuses frozen capture loading, `static_marker_offsets`,
shared trajectory IK and shared RMS calculation. It fits only original frames
$0,\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor,N-1$ of the existing pelvis segment. All four markers
must be observed. First-frame offsets impose a reference gauge and are held
fixed thereafter; they are not measured anatomical attachment locations.
Three samples are neither continuous motion nor independent trials.

## Actual Exploratory Evidence and Limitations

A locally retained, hash-pinned public candidate with 520 muscles, 80 bodies,
549 forces, two constraints and 1348 continuous states completed the three-pose
diagnostic under OpenSim 4.6. Aggregate RMS was 37.704 mm; the final sample was
65.192 mm. Pelvis rotation reached its unchanged source bound. An earlier
unbounded LM attempt was rejected for exceeding that bound and is retained.
Native stations agreed with native frame transforms within $1.1\times10^{-14}$ m.
Detailed capture identities, offsets and pose arrays remain private.

This result does not distinguish anatomical infeasibility from unresolved
fixed capture-to-model frame/yaw registration. Any registration must be estimated
from declared training anchors, frozen before independent evaluation and retained
in the identity. The near-zero first-frame error is constructed by calibration.
World/ground alignment, donor landmark semantics, nonpelvic bindings, subject
anthropometry, independent capture ancestry, noise/events, wrists, grip, passive
muscle loads, reserves, contact and full-state muscle replay remain open.
No source geometry or anatomy was modified to obtain this result.

## Reproduction and Runtime Isolation

Run the native tests serially with an installed OpenSim runtime:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -o addopts='' tests/opensim/test_native_marker_geometry.py tests/opensim/test_native_pelvis_probe_contract.py tests/unit/motion_matching/test_trajectory_coordinate_bounds.py
python3 -m scripts.diagnostics.native_pelvis_geometry --model MODEL.osim --model-sha256 SHA256 --capture FROZEN.c3d --capture-python C3D_PYTHON --output PRIVATE_RECEIPT.json
```

The Windows OpenSim and ezc3d wheels loaded incompatible DLL symbols together
in the tested process. The diagnostic therefore runs the existing frozen loader
in a separate SDK process and transfers through the existing TRC writer/reader.
It records source/TRC hashes and rounding (at most $5.1\times10^{-7}$ m and
$5.1\times10^{-10}$ s), validates labels/frame count, and restores the exact
frozen source clock. It introduces no new capture parser, interpolation or
retiming. Native execution clocks and independent replay are outside this probe.

Tests include analytic rigid transforms, physical offset frames, actual native
coupler assembly and dependent-range rejection, source-bound preservation,
missing-observation rejection and placeholder evidence rejection. They do not
qualify plugins, scientific uncertainty or whole-model muscle dynamics. Canonical
inventory, generated LaTeX/PDF parity, page review and publication remain blocked.
